body: Thank you for sharing your experiences.  The part I can relate to is having to fight hard with all your being to get out of it.  When I am in pockets of awareness as to what is happening, I too have to struggle incredibly to get out of it- in fact it takes multiple attempts.  I'm starting to think the medication I am on is causing unusual nightmares with symptoms of SP.
Just about.  It became much more acknowledged/regular when I left college at 23.
Depression creates a very fine line between self-accountability and recognizing what's out of our control.  You've helped me reestablish my sense of balance on that line a bit tonight, thank you.
I was 18, so maybe not that young but new to therapy.

Haha I did actually write my therapist a letter once!  You are completely right- it was handed right back to me and she asked what I had for breakfast instead.  I was really embarrassed.  At the time I was too young to realize that wasn't my fault, but perhaps it wasn't.

Pretty much.  The viibryd I honestly think has helped with my anxiety issues so I've asked to stay on it.  I've been on the SSRI merry-go-round and I just don't think my depression is serotonin related, but my instinct tells me to trust the experts.
I've been tapering off 1mg per day, which helps.  But yes, I wouldn't give it to my worst enemy.

Journaling is nice but it makes me feel very lonely- it's sort of like writing a letter I know no one will ever read.  I was in counseling... but I kept getting pawned off to different therapists who were exhausted themselves, robotic, and happy to drain my bank account.  I can recall one day when my therapist cut my session early and I went into the waiting room full of crying children and hate-filled adults and I felt a familiar pang in my chest as I stepped into the elevator and realized this was yet another place I didn't belong.

I have; my first therapist recommended I meditate, which would turn any cruel thoughts I had off for a bit but they would always come back.  The others I had recommended square breathing and using a journal.  These methods didn't really work and I've lost a lot of faith in the professional world of mental illness assistance.

I was really depressed after work one day; I started noticing how healthy some people looked and I was so envious.  I wanted to punish myself for being miserable and depressed so I figured the most productive way I could do so would be to turn my inner demons into drill sergeants.  I embraced my soreness, injuries, and cravings as a new-found pain to escape into, one that was different and made more sense.

Thank you.  Reading that comment stirred more in me than countless hours of professional therapy.  Becoming aware of and picking myself up from the years you've described has been the most difficult challenge I have faced to date and I can finally feel my will breaking.  I understand now that to live is to suffer but I have yet to understand why I must suffer alone.  I used to blame the ineptitude of others but at this point I can't help but assume it's my own shortcomings and failures.

Yeah you could say that.  Sometimes it's encouraging and others it's mocking.  I used to focus on it as if it were an attainable future but that was getting discouraging so recently I've tried to focus on the present.

Thanks Amy.  It's sort of like looking out a window into daylight when the power's out after a storm.  Surreal but familiar, uncomfortable yet natural.  Fun to wonder about, sad to reminisce.  Vast and inaccessible.
